idea-plugin.name: Spring Config Drift Inspector
idea-plugin.description:
Catch broken environment configuration before it reaches production. This plugin compares every application*.yml and application*.properties file across your profiles and reports what a code review alone tends to miss.

What it finds

  • Missing keys — set in some environments, silently absent from others, with default-profile inheritance handled correctly
  • Shape drift — the same key is a number in one environment and a string, list, or nested object in another
  • Exposed secrets — passwords, tokens, API keys, private keys, and credentials embedded in URLs. Values are masked the moment they are detected and are never stored, logged, or written to a report
  • Unresolved placeholders — ${DB_HOST} references with no default and nothing in the project to supply them
  • Metadata contract violations — cross-checked against spring-configuration-metadata.json for keys declared but never set, set but never declared, and simple type mismatches

Relaxed binding is understood, so driver-class-name, driverClassName, and DRIVER_CLASS_NAME count as one property rather than three. Profiles that only override a handful of keys are recognised as partial overlays instead of being reported as incomplete environments, and that judgement can be overridden per profile in settings.

Every finding jumps to the exact key in the exact file. Results export as Markdown for a pull request or JSON for a CI gate.

Scope

This is static comparison plus a lightweight metadata contract check — it does not reimplement the Spring Binder, analyse @ConfigurationProperties classes, resolve SpEL, Vault, or Config Server values, read your real environment variables, or modify your files.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
0.1.1

  • Fixed a race where dismissing a finding while an automatic re-analysis was in flight could make the dismissed finding silently reappear
  • Fixed a performance issue where every VFS change event in the IDE (not just config file changes) triggered a virtual file resolution, needlessly on the EDT
  • Fixed a caching bug where a metadata file that failed to read once could stay incorrectly cached as empty until its next unrelated change
  • Fixed a potential crash in the Key Matrix tool window when the profile set changes
  • Config file discovery order is now deterministic across runs
  • The Copy Report toolbar buttons now show a brief confirmation when the report is copied to the clipboard
  • "Analyze Spring Config Drift" is now also available by right-clicking an application*.yml/.properties file, in the Project view or the editor
  • A partial-overlay finding's Location column now names the Settings page it jumps to, instead of showing "—" as if the row led nowhere

0.1.0

  • First release: cross-profile comparison of YAML and properties configuration
  • Missing key, shape drift, secret exposure, unresolved placeholder, and metadata contract detection
  • Findings and key-matrix tool window with jump-to-source
  • Markdown and JSON report export
  • Partial-overlay profile detection, overridable in Settings | Tools | Config Drift

action.description: Compare application config files across profiles and report drift
